record.paper_title: Mapping current and activity fluctuations in exclusion processes: consequences and open questions
record.context_brief: Coordinate Bethe Ansatz crossover from EW to KPZ scaling
record.original_question: For the coordinate Bethe Ansatz description of SSEP activity fluctuations, how does the solution cross over from the Edwards-Wilkinson scaling regime, with s = λ/L² at fixed λ and large L, to the KPZ scaling regime, with finite s and large L?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the symmetric simple exclusion process (SSEP) on a periodic ring of L sites: each site is either empty or occupied by at most one particle, and each particle attempts, at rate 1, to jump to a uniformly chosen nearest neighbor, the move being accepted only if the target site is empty. The (time-integrated) dynamical activity K_t is the total number of particle jumps (in either direction) performed in the time interval [0,t]. Tilting the dynamics by a parameter s, one defines the scaled cumulant generating function

  ψ(s) = lim_{t→∞} (1/t) log E[ exp(s K_t) ],

which can be obtained as the largest eigenvalue of the tilted Markov generator

  (M_s f)(η) = Σ_{⟨i,j⟩} [ e^{s} η_i (1-η_j) f(η^{ij}) − η_i (1-η_j) f(η) ],

where η^{ij} denotes the configuration with the occupations at sites i and j swapped. The tilted generator is integrable and can be diagonalized by the coordinate Bethe Ansatz, giving ψ(s) and the corresponding eigenstate as functions of Bethe roots solving a coupled system of algebraic equations on the ring.

Two scaling regimes are known for activity fluctuations in the limit L → ∞:

  (i) Edwards–Wilkinson (EW) regime: s = λ/L² with λ fixed; here ψ(s) scales diffusively, consistent with EW universality.
  (ii) Kardar–Parisi–Zhang (KPZ) regime: s held fixed of order one with L → ∞; here ψ(s) exhibits KPZ-type scaling.

Problem. Starting from the coordinate Bethe Ansatz equations for the SSEP tilted by s, determine analytically how the structure of the Bethe roots and the resulting scaled cumulant generating function ψ(s,L) interpolates between these two regimes as the scaling of s with L is varied. In particular, identify an appropriate crossover scaling variable interpolating between s ∼ L^{-2} (EW) and s = O(1) (KPZ), and derive the corresponding crossover scaling function for ψ together with the asymptotic behavior of the Bethe roots in this crossover.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search returns the EW and KPZ scaling regimes for SSEP activity fluctuations as established phenomena, and ongoing work on Bethe-Ansatz analyses of current/activity fluctuations in periodic exclusion processes (e.g., 2024–2025 works on KPZ fluctuations in finite volume and on TASEP-ring scaling). However, no source was found that explicitly derives the coordinate Bethe Ansatz crossover scaling function bridging the EW (s=λ/L²) and KPZ (finite s) regimes for SSEP activity, so the question appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Mapping current and activity fluctuations in exclusion processes
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses EW vs KPZ scaling regimes for SSEP activity fluctuations and lists the crossover via coordinate Bethe Ansatz as an open question.
status_evidence.claim: The crossover between EW and KPZ regimes via coordinate Bethe Ansatz is highlighted as an open direction.

status_evidence.title: KPZ fluctuations in finite volume
status_evidence.snippet: Lecture notes (2024) on Bethe-Ansatz approaches to KPZ fluctuations in periodic systems.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to study Bethe-Ansatz-based finite-volume KPZ scaling, but does not resolve the SSEP EW–KPZ activity crossover.

status_evidence.title: Scaling Properties of Current Fluctuations in Periodic TASEP
status_evidence.snippet: 2025 work on scaling of current fluctuations in periodic TASEP.
status_evidence.claim: Related but does not address the SSEP activity EW-to-KPZ crossover via coordinate Bethe Ansatz.
